newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins rise as Eurobond launched.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins rise as Eurobond launched.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds showed an overall rise on Thursday on news of Russia's new Eurobond and the unfreezing of some MinFins.
But dealers said both events had already been partly priced into the market and some operators were taking profits.
Joint lead managers J.P. Morgan and SBC Warburg said on Thursday a $1.0 billion five-year Eurobond would be priced to yield 345 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.

Mikhail Ignatyev, a detective in the investigations department of the fifth central Moscow police precinct, told Reuters he had issued an order to unfreeze $56.81 million of MinFin bonds which he had frozen in June in connection with an investigation into the theft of securities.
"Trading started from higher levels than yesterday and prices rose further on both news," Most Bank dealer Alexander Rodionov said.
Dealers said support and resistance levels of all MinFin tranches were in the course of the day at 83.70-84.40, 60.80-61.50, 42.80-43.70, 48.70-49.20 and 36.70-37.40 respectively.
They added that Russian banks were mainly seen taking profits on the Eurobond news, while Western banks were buying, though not very actively.
Eurobank dealer Olivier Coursault said: "Today somebody was selling on news after buying on rumours before."
Dealers said MinFin bond prices could firm after the Eurobonds started trading since their spread over Treasuries was likely to tighten, given high subscription volumes.
"The market was delighted by the Eurobond issue. It is oversubscribed and its spread may be better... The Eurobond may drag up the prices of MinFins," Coursault said.
He added that the fourth tranche, closest in terms to the Eurobond, was likely to be the most favoured.
